We audit how KV-cache eviction affects reasoning accuracy when a model writes its own reasoning and when it answers from a supplied reasoning trace. On MATH-500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, we compare free-running accuracy with answer readout on a fixed full-cache trace, then replay compressed traces under a full cache as a complementary comparison. On 100 problems with four seeds each, protecting the prompt reduces the forward residual---the accuracy change unexplained by on-reference readout---while a negative residual remains for Random and StreamingLLM. With the prompt protected, the two replay directions disagree at the tighter budget of 256 entries (median nominal budget ratios $0.097$ for Random and $0.098$ for StreamingLLM). At a budget of 1024 entries (median nominal budget ratios $0.434$ and $0.487$), the protected forward residual is $-0.047$ (95\% CI $[-0.086,-0.015]$) for Random and $-0.040$ ($[-0.070,-0.013]$) for StreamingLLM; a direction interaction was not detected. On a strict-fit subset of 97 problems, prompt protection changes Random's free-running accuracy contrasts with both StreamingLLM and an H2O-style policy. These comparisons motivate reporting free-running accuracy alongside fixed-trace readout and specifying which prompt entries eviction can remove.

We audit how KV-cache eviction affects reasoning accuracy when a model writes its own reasoning and when it answers from a supplied reasoning trace. On MATH-500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, we compare free-running accuracy with answer readout on a fixed full-cache trace, then replay compressed traces under a full cache as a complementary comparison. On 100 problems with four seeds each, protecting the prompt reduces the forward residual---the accuracy change unexplained by on-reference readout---while a negative residual remains for Random and StreamingLLM. With the prompt protected, the two replay directions disagree at the tighter budget of 256 entries (median nominal budget ratios $0.097$ for Random and $0.098$ for StreamingLLM). At a budget of 1024 entries (median nominal budget ratios $0.434$ and $0.487$), the protected forward residual is $-0.047$ (95\% CI $[-0.086,-0.015]$) for Random and $-0.040$ ($[-0.070,-0.013]$) for StreamingLLM; a direction interaction was not detected. On a strict-fit subset of 97 problems, prompt protection changes Random's free-running accuracy contrasts with both StreamingLLM and an H2O-style policy. These comparisons motivate reporting free-running accuracy alongside fixed-trace readout and specifying which prompt entries eviction can remove.
